main_text.l: TERRA restat Elementum grave, crassissimum, siccum, aridum, opacum, firmum & stabile in medio Universi libratum.

l.i: Geographis terra est medium & unum totius Universitatis, rotunda, immobilis.
Fallopio terra est omne illud, quod effoditur, & addito humido primò emollescit, fitq; lutum, mox aucto humido eliquatur dissolvitur-ve.
Peripato Terra est simplex corpus, seu ut Casparus Contarenus ait, terra est nullibi & nulla sui parte simplex, præterquàm circa centrum.
S. Scriptura vocat Aridam. Sicca est, quia affusum humorem combibens suapte natura exsiccat.
Hac tametsi partibus constet solidis, intrinsecus tamen suos habet meatus, sinus & cavernas, quæ recipiunt fumum quasi spiritum, aquam & humores quasi sanguinem.
Vulgò fertur esse frigida, at ita esse terram frigidam, ut omnis caloris sit expers, rectè

page.notes: The first letter of TERRA is a large woodcut initial E, joined to the following RRA. Faint show-through text in both margins and at the top of the page is ignored. The mark after "centrum" is a printed ornament, transcribed as a stop. The word "Vulgò" is printed with a letter that looks like K in the scan, read as V. The catchword "nega-" is at the bottom right.
